text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N2","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE:- 1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 28-32 HRC. 2) THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT 3) REMOVE ALL SHARP EDGES & CORNERS."}],"comment":"The note specifies the hardness range and that threads must be kept soft, but it does not state at which manufacturing stage the heat treatment is to be applied (e.g., before or after final machining of the keyways and threads). Without a defined sequence the machinist cannot plan operations correctly, risking distortion of finished features. Add the process stage to N2, for example 'TO BE TOUGHENED AFTER ROUGH MACHINING, BEFORE FINAL GRINDING AND THREADING.'.","recommended_correction":"Update note N2 to specify the manufacturing stage at which the 28-32 HRC toughening applies relative to machining and threading."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"surface_treatment","page":1,"quote":"IZBP"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D2","page":1,"quote":"-0.009"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D3","page":1,"quote":"-0.025"}],"comment":"The title block calls out IZBP plating, and dimensions D2/D3 define a tolerance band of 0.016 mm on a shaft diameter, yet no allowance is made for the plating thickness. Plating will add material and push the finished shaft outside its tight tolerance, preventing proper assembly with the mating bore. The designer should either reduce the basic size by the expected plating thickness or add a note specifying pre-plate machining limits." ,"recommended_correction":"Reduce the nominal shaft diameter or add a note accounting for IZBP plating thickness so the finished plated dimension remains within the -0.009/-0.025 tolerance band."}]}
